Rolling-Window LPPLS Calibration (rolling \(T_1\), fixed \(T_2\))

Source: R/lppls_rolling.R
lppls_rolling.Rd

Calibrates a sequence of LPPLS models that share a common calibration end \(T_2\) while the start time \(T_1\) rolls over t1_seq. This is the multi-window primitive underlying both the window-diagnostic plots (rolling_tc_plot(), rolling_param_plot()) and Lagrange regularization (lppls_lagrange()): the (expensive) calibrations are computed once here and reused by all downstream analyses.

Usage

lppls_rolling(
  log_price,
  t1_seq,
  hold_out = 0,
  fh = 30,
  tc_init = NULL,
  fit_args = list(),
  fb = FALSE
)

Arguments

log_price

Numeric vector of log-prices for the full series.

t1_seq

Integer vector of rolling start indices (absolute positions into log_price). All entries must be < T2 = length(log_price) - hold_out.

hold_out

Integer, number of observations reserved from the end of the full series for the forecast/validation region (default 0). Fixes \(T_2\).

fh

Integer, forecast horizon passed to fit_lppls() (default 30).

tc_init

Numeric or NULL. Initial critical time for fit_lppls(). If NULL (default) a per-window value n_cal + floor(fh / 2) is used, where n_cal is the window's calibration length.

fit_args

Named list of additional arguments forwarded to fit_lppls() (e.g. lower, upper, m_init, o_init, num_searches, mode, mpl_cutoff, factr). The arguments log_price, fh, hold_out, tc_init and fb are controlled by lppls_rolling() and are ignored if supplied here. If mode is not supplied it defaults to "MPL".

fb

Logical, whether to print per-window feedback (default FALSE).

Value

An object of class "lppls_rolling": a list with

table

Data frame with one row per window: T1, n_cal, the absolute point estimates tc, m, omega, A, B, C1, C2, D, the calibration-region residual sum of squares sse_cal, the absolute likelihood-interval bounds LI5l/LI5u/LI10l/LI10u/LI50l/LI50u and the absolute modified-profile-likelihood estimate tc_hat_mpl.

fits

List of best-fit parameter lists (fit[[1]]) per window, in window-local time.

t1_seq, T2, hold_out, fh, n_full

The calibration setup.

fit_args

The effective list of arguments forwarded to fit_lppls() (after stripping the controlled ones and defaulting mode); recorded so lr_trend_test() can re-roll bootstrap replicates with the same settings.

Details

For each \(T_1\) in t1_seq the model is calibrated on log_price[T1:length(log_price)] via fit_lppls(). The last hold_out observations of every window are reserved for the forecast/validation region, so the calibration region is the absolute interval \([T_1, T_2]\) with the common end \(T_2 = \texttt{length(log\_price)} - \texttt{hold\_out}\) held fixed across windows.

Because fit_lppls() re-indexes each window to start at 1, all per-window results (tc, the likelihood intervals and tc_hat_mpl) are shifted back to absolute time by adding \(T_1 - 1\) before being returned.

The likelihood-interval columns (LI5l ... tc_hat_mpl) are populated only when the fit is run in mode = "MPL" (the default); under mode = "F2" they are NA but the point estimates and sse_cal (hence Lagrange) are identical.

Profiling on macOS

mode defaults to "MPL", so profiling a rolling calibration on macOS hits the R-profiler/Accelerate crash described under "Profiling mode = \"MPL\" on macOS" in fit_lppls(). The same options(matprod = "internal") workaround applies. Unprofiled runs are unaffected.

See also

fit_lppls(), lppls_lagrange(), rolling_tc_plot(), rolling_param_plot()

Examples

## A simulated bubble: 300 observations of an LPPLS path whose critical time
## is t = 301
set.seed(3630)
N     <- 300
log_p <- eval_lppls(seq_len(N), A = 8, B = -0.025, C1 = 0.0015, C2 = 0.001,
                    tc = N + 1, m = 0.6, omega = 8) + rnorm(N) * 0.01

## Five windows whose start T1 rolls forward from 1 to 101, all ending at
## T2 = 280. MPL mode gives the likelihood intervals rolling_tc_plot() draws.
roll <- lppls_rolling(
  log_price = log_p,
  t1_seq    = seq(from = 1, by = 25, length.out = 5),
  hold_out  = 20, fh = 30,
  fit_args  = list(lower = c(0.1, 6, -0.03, 0.8),
                   upper = c(0.9, 13, -1e-14, 1e6),
                   m_init = 0.5, o_init = 8, num_searches = 1,
                   mode = "MPL")
)
roll
#> LPPLS rolling-window calibration
#>   Windows (T1):  5  (from 1 to 101, step 25)
#>   T2 (cal. end): 280
#>   hold_out: 20   fh: 30
#>   Likelihood intervals: present (MPL)
rolling_tc_plot(roll)
